clue.text: Constable possibly showing signs of running, having nabbed one

indicators.note: to nab is to grab hold of, so the running word closes around the extra letter

parts.note: heavy breathing is what running shows
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A police constable, out of breath from a chase, has caught somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C hides the painter John Constable behind a police officer; PANTING takes in I to give PAINTING.
explanation.definitionFit: A work by the English landscape artist John Constable is an example of a painting, which 'possibly' signals.

clue.text: A slippery customer, prisoner's hiding in country, not caught

indicators.note: something hiding in a place is tucked inside it
caught is C in cricket scoring, and not having it means that letter is taken out

parts.note: the North American country
a con is a convict

explanation.surface: An escaped convict is lying low abroad, still at large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Customer' suggests a person, but a slippery customer here is a snake. Caught is C in cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: An anaconda is a huge, smooth-scaled snake, so it is literally a slippery creature.

clue.text: It lets you round down to the nearest digit

definitions.text: It lets you round down to the nearest digit

parts.words: round down to the nearest digit
parts.note: the surface reading is arithmetic: rounding a number down to the nearest whole figure
the setter means a tool that lets you shape and shorten the tip of a finger, a digit in the other sense

explanation.surface: A gadget or rule for rounding numbers down to a whole figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Digit means finger as well as figure; a nail file rounds and shortens a nail right down to the fingertip.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail file is the small abrasive tool used to shape fingernails into a rounded edge.

clue.text: Comment from protestor left out in Scottish island

indicators.note: out means removed, so the named letter leaves the island's name

parts.note: Islay is a Hebridean island famous for whisky
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A demonstrator's remark about someone being left behind on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: ISLAY without its L leaves ISAY.
explanation.definitionFit: "I say!" is a dated British exclamation of objection or surprise, the sort of thing an indignant protester calls out.

clue.text: Decoration that's both good and rubbish

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
litter is rubbish dropped in the street

explanation.surface: An ornament that is somehow both lovely and trashy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jokes about tacky ornaments; G then LITTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Glitter is the sparkly material sprinkled on cards and costumes as ornament.

clue.text: Armaments one manufactured in conventional activities

indicators.note: something manufactured is assembled from parts, so these letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Weapons are being produced as part of conventional warfare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conventional' suggests conventional (non-nuclear) arms; it is the definition, meaning ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: The mainstream is the body of ordinary, accepted activity and opinion, as opposed to the fringe.

clue.text: Donation raised before political group's attack

indicators.note: raised means lifted upward, and in a down entry that reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: aid is help given, such as a donation
a tribe is a faction or political grouping

explanation.surface: A gift is collected ahead of a party's political assault.
explanation.walkthrough: AID reads upward as DIA; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a forceful piece of criticism.

clue.text: When knight goes topless, then may the ladies rejoice

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top, and in a down entry the top of each word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written, then losing its top letter
taken as written, then losing its top letter

explanation.surface: Women celebrate when a knight strips off his top.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'When' and 'knight' drop their first letters. A hen night is the British bachelorette party, the bride's night out with women friends; the surface hints at a male stripper.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen night is a women-only celebration before a wedding, an occasion for ladies to rejoice.

clue.text: It may quantify how a tanker is laden with oil at sea

definitions.text: It may quantify how a tanker is laden with oil at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and all over the place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note on how much crude oil a tanker is carrying out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty as definition and wordplay. A load line, or Plimsoll line, is the mark on a ship's hull showing how deep it may legally sit when loaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A load line (Plimsoll line) is the hull marking that gauges how heavily a ship is loaded, so it measures how laden a tanker is.

clue.text: Fish I'm keeping hot, twice sent back

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
to keep something is to hold it inside, so the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: I'm expanded to I am
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
twice means the finished chunk is written out a second time

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their fish warm but it keeps being returned to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: I AM holding H gives IHAM; turned round that is MAHI, and doing it twice gives MAHI-MAHI.
explanation.definitionFit: The mahi-mahi, also called dorado or dolphinfish, is a large ocean game fish common on restaurant menus.

clue.text: Two animals unite — here's an elementary alternative

definitions.text: Two animals unite — here's an elementary alternative

parts.note: read on the surface as two creatures joining forces; the setter means two animal words joined into the other name of a metal
elementary means of a chemical element: the answer is the alternative name for that same element

explanation.surface: Two creatures team up, offered as a simple option.
explanation.walkthrough: WOLF and RAM joined make WOLFRAM, which is the other name for the element TUNGSTEN (hence its symbol W); the answer is the alternative to the name the animals build.
explanation.definitionFit: Tungsten and wolfram are two names for the same chemical element, so one is the elementary alternative to the other.

clue.text: Footballer's remanded at port

parts.note: someone remanded in custody is inside, slang for in prison
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A footballer has been remanded in custody at a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like a harbour town; it is the nautical left. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside left was a forward position in the classic football formation, so a player in that role is a footballer.

clue.text: Concerning current vote on states

parts.note: to vote someone in is to elect them
two US states: RI (Rhode Island) and CAL (California)

explanation.surface: A note about the vote currently being held across the states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present'; it is electric current. 'On' places the vote above the states in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical describes anything to do with electricity, the flow of current through a wire.

clue.text: Part of aircraft seen to oscillate: front falling off

indicators.note: the front dropping away means the opening letter of the word is lost

parts.note: to oscillate is to sway back and forth

explanation.surface: An aircraft part wobbles alarmingly until its nose drops off.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the S from the front of SWING to leave WING.
explanation.definitionFit: The wings are the main lifting surfaces of an aeroplane, so a wing is one component of it.

clue.text: Turned round bureaucracy, up to a point

indicators.note: turning a phrase round here swaps its two halves, moving the back part to the front

parts.note: red tape is the officialdom of forms and procedures

explanation.surface: Someone has partly overcome the paperwork of officialdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up to a point' reads as 'partly'; it means narrowing to a point. RED TAPE with its halves swapped gives TAPE RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tapered narrows gradually to a point, like a candle or a spire.

clue.text: Methodically arrange sacred dead

parts.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, forbidden as sacred
the late someone is someone dead

explanation.surface: A careful arranging of holy remains.
explanation.walkthrough: TABU is an older spelling of taboo, meaning set apart as holy.
explanation.definitionFit: To tabulate data is to set it out systematically in a table.

clue.text: One taking off dirt with soap in a lather

indicators.note: in a lather means agitated and flustered, so these letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone scrubbing off grime with plenty of soapy suds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' looks like removing dirt; it means mimicking, and 'lather' fits the washing picture while signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is British slang for imitating them, which is what a parodist does for comic effect.

clue.text: Ask men to lead search

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the first piece is placed ahead of the second

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of soldiers
a quest is a long search

explanation.surface: A request that the men head up the search party.
explanation.walkthrough: Men as RE (Royal Engineers) is a common crossword convention for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To request something is to ask for it politely; both are verbs of seeking.

clue.text: Brought down from The Mount

parts.note: the capitals suggest the Sermon on the Mount, as if a teaching were carried down a hill
the setter means a rider thrown from the horse that serves as a mount

explanation.surface: Something carried down from a biblical hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals are surface decoration; a mount is a horse, and being brought down from it means being thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unhorsed has been knocked off their horse, the animal they were riding.

clue.text: Curved form of tendon seen on bird class, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a sinew is a tendon
Aves is the zoological class of birds

explanation.surface: A biology note on the curving tendons found in most birds.
explanation.walkthrough: AVES is the Latin class name for birds; losing its last letter leaves AVE. 'On' places the tendon above it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sine wave is the smooth, regularly undulating curve plotted by the sine function.

clue.text: Note one's found in manuscripts

parts.note: the surface suggests a musical note written in old handwritten scores
the setter means a letter sitting exactly at the centre of the word manuscripts, described in the answer's own words

explanation.surface: A musical note that turns up in old handwritten scores.
explanation.walkthrough: MANUSCRIPTS has eleven letters and the sixth, its exact centre, is C: so the C is in the middle, and MIDDLE C is also a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle C is the note near the centre of the piano keyboard, the reference pitch for beginners.

clue.text: Having last drop of lager in bar, returned this?

definitions.text: Having last drop of lager in bar, returned this?

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the word for bar is read backwards
in places the single letter inside the other word

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: the last drop is the final bit, so only the closing letter of the word is used

parts.note: the final letter of lager

explanation.surface: After draining the last of the lager in a pub, someone brings up gas.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: PUB turned round is BUP, and R goes in to make BURP, what the drinker returned.
explanation.definitionFit: A burp is gas brought back up from the stomach, typically after a fizzy drink like lager.

clue.text: Victor may be an old car with only half a horn

indicators.note: only half means the word is cut down to its first half

parts.note: Triumph was a British car maker, defunct since the 1980s
an antler is a deer's horn

explanation.surface: Victor drives an old car whose horn has half broken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' looks like a man's name; it is any winner. Halving ANTLER leaves ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A winner is often jubilant after victory, so 'may be' introduces an adjective describing a victor.

clue.text: Robin beside Windermere, say, in old children's book

parts.note: Lady Windermere is the title character of Oscar Wilde's play Lady Windermere's Fan; 'say' marks an example of a lady
a robin is a bird

explanation.surface: A robin by Lake Windermere features in a vintage picture book.
explanation.walkthrough: Windermere looks like the Lake District lake, but here it is a title, as in Wilde's Lady Windermere.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladybird Books were the classic small hardback British children's books of the mid-twentieth century.

clue.text: Aim to get every second out of middleman

indicators.note: every second means taking the letter in each even position and skipping the others

parts.note: letters two, four, six and eight of middleman

explanation.surface: The goal is to squeeze every second of value from a broker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every second' looks like time; it is a letter-by-letter instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea can mean an intention or purpose, as in 'the idea is to win', so it matches aim.

clue.text: Casanova succeeded splitting couple?

indicators.note: splitting means forcing apart, so the single letter goes into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: a couple as a woman and a man; the question mark flags this playful reading
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: A notorious seducer succeeded in breaking up a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a couple is being read as one lady and one man.
explanation.definitionFit: Casanova was the famous Venetian seducer, so his name stands for any womaniser who charms women.

clue.text: Check luggage for new suit?

parts.note: to check something is to test it
a case is a piece of luggage

explanation.surface: Someone inspects their suitcase before packing a new suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like clothing; it is a lawsuit, as the question mark hints.
explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a lawsuit brought to set a legal precedent, a new kind of legal action.

clue.text: Author caught coach

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a handler trains and manages an animal or a fighter

explanation.surface: A writer is picked up by a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a bus; it is a trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler was the American crime novelist who created the detective Philip Marlowe.
